description: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026'ya katılan, yenilikçi ve hedef odaklı bir ekibiz. NASA uydu verileri, yapay zekâ ve teknolojiyi birleştirerek sürdürülebilir tarım alanında etkili bir çözüm geliştirmeyi hedefliyoruz. Ekibimiz hazır, vizyonumuz net ve çalışan bir prototip ortaya koymaya kararlıyız. Yazılım, yapay zekâ, veri bilimi, mühendislik ve çevre bilimleri alanlarına ilgi duyan, üretmeyi seven katılımcılarla tanışmak isteriz.
summary:
FARM COMPASS · Project Summary
Farmers need to know what they can do for their fields today. Agricultural engineers need to see the data and assumptions behind each recommendation. We built Farm Compass to give both groups the same field data in a form that meets their needs.

Users can select a field anywhere in the world on an interactive map. Farm Compass brings together NASA POWER climate data, regional soil information, and historical records of natural hazards. It shows which crops suit the field, how local climate conditions shape those recommendations, and which risks to consider, including late frost, drought, and erosion.

The Daily Guide helps farmers compare suitable crops and decide what to plant next season. A voice assistant gives them hands-free access to field information while they work. The Analysis Center gives agricultural engineers access to soil maps, crop rotation comparisons, estimates of soil carbon and nitrogen balance, and long-term scenarios. With the sources and assumptions behind each result visible, engineers can spend less time gathering data and more time evaluating options. Both groups can better understand their fields and plan for future seasons.
details:
Farmers manage their land while facing a changing climate and natural hazards that can be hard to predict. Choosing the best way to use a field means weighing many combinations of crops, planting dates, water needs, and local risks. Sorting through those options takes time, and a poorly matched choice can cost money for an entire season. We built Farm Compass to turn large, scattered datasets into clear guidance for farmers and detailed, traceable analysis for agricultural engineers.

Users start by drawing their field boundary on an interactive map. Farm Compass retrieves NASA POWER climate data for that location and combines it with regional soil information and historical hazard records. It compares local conditions with each crop’s growing requirements to rank crops by a suitability score out of 100, suggest planting times, and estimate how much of each crop’s seasonal water requirement rainfall may leave unmet. The Daily Guide explains these results in plain language, helping farmers focus on crops that fit their land.

The Crop Rotation Planner uses field data and the farmer’s priorities, such as saving water, protecting the soil, or reducing risk, to compare planting sequences. It shows which crop to plant and when, identifies gaps between main crops, and checks where a winter cover crop fits. Farmers can compare the suggested rotation with their current plan and see why the model favors one sequence over another.

The Field Monitoring Panel organizes climate, soil, terrain, and risk data in one place. Agricultural engineers can review the field at a glance, then explore soil organic carbon maps, modeled nitrogen balances, historical climate records, and 10-year scenarios. This gives them more time to evaluate alternatives and less time to gather data across platforms. When configured, Telegram alerts can notify users about events flagged by supported data sources, such as severe weather or nearby earthquakes. With GPS permission, Voice Field Mode can read out information and recommendations for the part of the field where the user is working.

The International Space Station’s closed-loop water recovery system inspired Resource Loss Analysis. Users enter how much irrigation water, nitrogen, and pump energy they used over a selected period. Farm Compass estimates how much served its intended purpose and how much remained unused under the selected assumptions. The ISS water recovery figure provides a reference as we explore which principles of resource recovery and reuse could be adapted to farming.

The Frequency Protocol connects to an Arduino-controlled buzzer and plays selectable test frequencies for future experiments on plant responses to drought and pest behavior. Its agricultural effects have yet to be tested in the field. We built the desktop application with Python and Tkinter, used JavaScript and Leaflet for interactive maps, and connected the Arduino prototype through pySerial. Farm Compass identifies its data sources, model estimates, and sample data so users can see what each result is based on before making a decision.
